title: FlashProve-Next Proves LLM API Responses in 1.49 Seconds
summary: FlashProve-Next attaches zero-knowledge proofs to LLM API responses in 1.49s, letting clients verify model identity without exposing weights or activations.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- FlashProve-Next generates zero-knowledge proofs for LLM API responses in 1.49 seconds on vLLM Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 deployments.
- The system verifies model identity, precision, and reasoning budget without exposing weights, prompts, or activations to clients.
- Twenty-eight Lean 4 modules with 696 declarations mechanize soundness, with zero false rejections across 1.85 million test blocks.


Officially launched on November 26, 2026, FlashProve-Next introduces a cryptographic verification layer for[closed-weight LLM](https://emergent.sh/glossary/closed-source-model) API responses, reporting 1.49-second proof generation on live vLLM Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 deployments with 23.4-millisecond Rust-side CPU verification. Author Liang Song open-sourced code, specifications, and benchmarks alongside a paper detailing zero-knowledge-masked proofs that let clients verify model identity, precision, and reasoning budget without exposing weights, hidden prompts, or activations.


The system addresses what Song frames as a trust gap: clients using closed-weight LLM APIs have no native way to confirm a provider ran the advertised model at the stated precision and reasoning budget. Existing approaches force operators to choose between hardware trust anchors, third-party auditors, or costly integer-surrogate re-proving that diverges from native floating-point serving paths.


## How FlashProve-Next Works


FlashProve-Next generates verifiable, zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual API responses without modifying native serving infrastructure. The system supports bf16, fp8, and mxfp4 precision; random sampling; FlashAttention; CUDA graphs; batching; and prefix caching. A non-depleting Reed-Solomon commitment binds the model identifier, and two verification modes carry explicit cryptographic error bounds: non-interactive public mode (NI-315) at error probability ε ≤ 2^-40, and external-seed mode (ExtSeed-153) at ε ≤ 2^-20.


The paper reports zero false rejections across five-model Blackwell calibration covering 1.85 million GEMM and mixture-of-experts blocks plus 1.96 million non-GEMM rows. The system also passes a 14-of-14 cheating matrix, though the abstract does not enumerate those 14 attack vectors.


## Performance Benchmarks and Formal Verification


The headline 1.49-second figure applies to proof generation on a live vLLM-served Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 deployment, with verification completing in 23.4 milliseconds on CPU. Proving a smaller Qwen3-0.6B model in ExtSeed-153 mode at unique-decoding Q=128 required 450.2 seconds of GPU time and 10.76 seconds on CPU. Song notes two current limitations: dense profiles fix coarse geometry, and cross-architecture hiding is deferred.


Twenty-eight Lean 4 modules containing 696 declarations mechanize the soundness proof with what the paper describes as "zero sorry, standard axioms only," meaning every proof step is completed without placeholders or unfinished obligations. This formal verification layer distinguishes FlashProve-Next from heuristic or audit-based approaches to API transparency.


## Release Details and Open-Source Availability


Officially released on November 26, 2026, FlashProve-Next ships with open-sourced code, formal specifications, and benchmark suites. The system runs on standard CUDA-enabled GPUs and integrates with vLLM deployments without requiring modifications to serving pipelines. Song published the work as a single-author preprint alongside the code release, positioning it within a broader ecosystem of 149 inference-layer projects tracked in the last 90 days focused on serving-side verifiability.


The release targets API providers seeking cryptographic guarantees for clients, researchers exploring zero-knowledge proof systems for machine learning, and enterprises requiring audit trails for model deployment. The 1.49-second overhead on 30-billion-parameter models suggests production feasibility for latency-tolerant workloads, though Song flags the need for further work on cross-architecture hiding and finer-grained geometry profiles.


## What This Means


FlashProve-Next shifts LLM API verification from trust-based or hardware-dependent models to cryptographic proof systems compatible with native serving infrastructure. The 1.49-second proof generation time and 23.4-millisecond verification overhead on 30-billion-parameter models position the system within production latency budgets for many use cases, while the Lean 4 formalization provides a mechanized soundness guarantee. As closed-weight APIs proliferate, cryptographic verification layers like FlashProve-Next offer a path toward client-side auditability without requiring weight disclosure or third-party intermediaries.
